subject: bat
pitch: A fruit bat with its wings spread wide. A fluffy golden-brown body, a fox-like face with big dark eyes and a moist black nose, pointed ears, and leathery charcoal wings stretched between long finger bones with a small hooked claw on each thumb. It clutches a half-eaten fig in its feet.
reasoning:
I'm designing a fruit bat in flight pose, wings spread and clutching a fig, working out how to ground it so its lowest point touches y=0.

I'm sketching the skeleton: a root body joint, a spine chain running from hips to chest, then neck and head joints with a jaw, all scaled to a roughly 0.2m body and 1m wingspan. I'm now planning the body geometry as a sweep over the spine chain with varying radii, considering small fluff details around the chest area.

Moving to the head, I'm planning a skull shape with a snout, nose, large eyes with highlights, ears, and a separate lower jaw piece. For the wings I'm laying out shoulder-elbow-wrist arm chains spread outward on each side, with a thumb claw and fanning finger digits extending from the wrist.

Working out finger tip positions for a batlike wingspan, fanning the digits from leading edge outward and backward with a slight droop, then connecting the trailing edge back toward the hips and legs.

Now I'm structuring the membranes: each finger forms a chain of joints from wrist through a mid-point to the tip, and I'll stretch membrane surfaces between consecutive finger chains, plus one connecting the arm to the first finger and another from the last finger down to the leg edge.

Still working out the membrane geometry...

Setting membrane thickness and mottled charcoal coloring for the wing texture, then setting up the arm and finger joint chains with proper parenting so the skeleton skins correctly.

Now I'm positioning the hind legs so they grip the fig, working out hip and foot coordinates relative to the fig and body placement, and adjusting the fig's vertical position so it sits properly below the body with the legs spanning a reasonable length between hip and foot.

Still working out toe placement...

With feet placed, toes sit nicely on top of the fig. Now for the fig itself I'm thinking of a teardrop sphere, purple-skinned (#5a2d4f), with a bitten section on the front face revealing pink-red flesh (#c8405a) — maybe approximating the bite as an intersecting or protruding shape rather than a true boolean cut.

Still figuring out the bite geometry...

Working out the hemisphere geometry...

Checking hip-to-foot distance confirms the leg bend works, then I'm sketching the body as a fluffy ellipsoid along a spine with three joints, tilting slightly upward toward the chest, and defining a radius function that varies smoothly along that spine.

I'm layering on countershaded golden-brown coloring with a cream belly and lighter ruff, then scattering spiky cone-shaped fur tufts across the body surface to give it a stylized, bristly texture before finalizing the swept body surface.

Now I'm adding a ring of larger pale spikes around the neck to form a chest ruff, positioning and tilting them outward along the neck joint line, then setting up the head joint position and orientation.

Working out head anatomy...

Positioning the lower jaw beneath the muzzle with its own joint parented to the head, keeping color simple for now and skipping extras like a tongue. Then adding a small black sphere at the muzzle tip for the nose.

Working out eye placement using a side-aware helper so left and right eyes mirror correctly, with dark glossy spheres and tiny white highlight spheres for shine.

For the ears, I'm sketching pointed cone shapes or extruded triangular outlines, positioning them to taper upward and outward with slight flattening so they read naturally from the front view.

I'll offset the inner ear forward in world space regardless of mirroring, and place ear bases relative to the head with a slight outward offset. For coloring, I'm giving the face a darker brown mask with lighter cheek tufts, keeping the skull a flat tan tone, and ensuring the neck sphere overlaps the chest before moving on to wing bone coloring.

Now I'm setting up membrane paint with a charcoal mottled look, building finger chains as slightly curved polylines by adding a small droop to the midpoint, and naming the wing joints uniquely per side for the arm and finger chains.

Working out arm and finger joint positions...

That's too large, so I'm scaling the wingtip coordinates down by .85 to get a more realistic 1.5m span for a flying fox, setting F1 through F4 and the wrist position accordingly. Now I'm working out the trailing membrane that connects the last finger to the hip/leg, figuring out the path points between wrist, knee, and ankle.

Checking that the inner membrane between the arm and the hip-wrist path doesn't overlap with the outer membrane between F4 and the trailing edge — they should form distinct, non-overlapping regions covering the plagiopatagium.

For path edges I'll specify the bone explicitly as the hips spine joint, since the chain side derives its bone naturally. The membrane color passes through as a paint option, and I'm mapping out the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root joint, spine chain with three named points parented to hips, and legs chain also parented to hips at their own root joints.

For legs, I'm defining three-point chains (hip, knee, foot) per side with named joints and default tip contacts. Fruit bats have no tail so I'm skipping that, and for the thumb I'm setting up a two-point chain from wrist to thumb tip, parented at the wrist with a digit role.

I'm shaping the hooked claw with a curved bezier dipping downward from the thumb tip, tapering radius to a point, colored ivory, and working out which joint in the thumb chain corresponds to the tip for bone attachment.

Now I'm setting up sweeps for the limb chains, then scattering fluff tufts over the body surface with a backward-leaning flow, plus a fluffy golden collar at the shoulders and cheek tufts on the head. I'm starting to build the body's paint using a countershaded mottle pattern.

Still building the skull and muzzle geometry...

Now for the jaw I'm sweeping a tapered radius shape from near the chin to the jaw tip, positioning it so the muzzle bottom slightly overlaps for a closed-mouth look, then considering posing the jaw bone with a small rotation to crack it open just a touch.

I should also add small fang details—tiny cone shapes, two up on the head and two down on the jaw—keeping them minimal and cheap to build.

For a fig detail, I'm layering concentric discs facing forward: a purple hemisphere base, then nested rings of flesh-pink, red, and dark core colors with tiny yellow seed spheres scattered across the surface, all slightly offset in z to avoid clipping. I still need to figure out which bone to attach the fig geometry to, since the figure is only rigged through the feet.

Checking the toe tips sit within the hemisphere bounds relative to center C, confirming the foot position stays mostly inside the sphere with just tips visible, and sketching small dark fur-colored spheres for the feet at adjusted coordinates.

I'm now working out four toe directions per foot with slight spread in x and z components, mirrored for left/right sides.

Setting claw spikes at each toe tip, skipping the eye socket detail. I'm sketching the sweep geometry for the muzzle and body (with faceted vs smooth sides), then placing a neck ruff ring near the chest with its position and radius.

Adding a second ruff layer with alternating colors, then working out cheek tufts as small spikes extending outward from the head using literal model-space direction vectors.

Now I'm shaping the ears with extruded outlines—a darker rim and a smaller pink inner outline—and sketching a simple scaled sphere for the eye.

I'm setting up wing membranes stretched between finger chains using a shared paint, plus fur sweeps along the legs and arms, and defining toe bones off the last leg joint. I'm double-checking that the figure's bounding box bottoms out correctly at the hemisphere base.

Now I'm sorting out the imports I need—builder, frame, rng, limb helpers, bezier for claws, and the mottle/countershade paint utilities with a lerp function.
